title: test:balancer-donation is ticked twice as the index-4 streamer regression test, but the script was never modified by story 073 and cannot exercise the streamer at all — it hand-rolls the PSM route and asserts against the batch minter, which is no longer where index-4 USDC lands
specText: Story 073 Change 2, line 505 (ticked): 'Update every batchMint( call site found in preflight to the 4-arg / length-3 minRewards form, re-fetching getNudgeTokens() rather than hardcoding 3.' Story 073 Verification line 539 (ticked): 'npm run test:nudge-payout and npm run test:balancer-donation pass against a fresh deploy (after their batchMint call sites are updated)'. Story 073 Verification line 538 (ticked), which frames the surrounding claim: 'Smoke-test a donation on each donor path — a Uniboost mint, an index-7 ratchet dispatch, a BalancerPoolerV2 batch donation and an SYA claim() — and assert collectNudge does not revert on any of them. **This is the direct regression test for the streamer-unset breakage.**'
faithfulnessRouting: F-01 — PRIMARY. Routed to the spec-conformance report at honest severity. MUST NOT be filed into the QA/gas bundle (Law 2).
description: script/interactions/TestBalancerDonation.s.sol is not touched by any of story 073's three commits (3fb4e34, d241e61, c054833); `git log` shows its last modification is 4c5c3cd [story-070]. Checklist lines 505 and 539 are nonetheless ticked, 505 asserting that every batchMint call site found in preflight was updated and 539 asserting that test:balancer-donation passes 'after their batchMint call sites are updated'. The script survives unmodified only because it never calls batchMint: grep confirms it contains no batchMint, collectNudge or nudgeStreamer reference. Instead it hand-rolls the donation route — :129 `psm.buyGem(batchNFTMinterAddr, gemAmt)` — and asserts `require(usdcDelta == gemAmt, "donation USDC mismatch")` at :135 against the BATCH MINTER's USDC balance. Post-story-073, the real index-4 donation routes USDC into the NudgeStreamer via collectNudge (DeployMocks.s.sol:779-784), not to the batch minter.
impact: A green `npm run test:balancer-donation` is consistent with the index-4 streamer being entirely unwired, so it proves nothing about the repair story 073 exists to deliver — while story line 538 explicitly directs the reader to treat this family of smoke tests as 'the direct regression test for the streamer-unset breakage'. The aggravating factor is which leg is masked: index-4 is the ONE leg where the pre-story breakage was SILENT, because `_dispatch`'s try/catch swallows the revert inside `_psmDonate` and the mint still succeeds (stated verbatim at DeployMocks.s.sol:779-781). The leg with no natural alarm is therefore the leg whose designated regression test cannot fail for the relevant reason. Story 072 inherits the same index-4 cutover and would inherit this test as its evidence of repair.
attackPath: No attack path. Verification-coverage gap: (1) story 073's three commits (3fb4e34, d241e61, c054833) do not touch script/interactions/TestBalancerDonation.s.sol — its last modification is 4c5c3cd [story-070] — yet checklist lines 505 and 539 are ticked as though it had been updated and re-run as part of this story's coverage.

(2) The script survives unmodified only because it never calls batchMint. It hand-rolls the route itself: :129 `psm.buyGem(batchNFTMinterAddr, gemAmt)`, then :135 `require(usdcDelta == gemAmt, "donation USDC mismatch")` measured against the BATCH MINTER's USDC balance. grep confirms it contains no reference to batchMint, collectNudge or nudgeStreamer.
(3) Post-story-073 the real index-4 donation no longer terminates at the batch minter: BalancerPoolerV2 routes USDC into the NudgeStreamer via collectNudge (wired at DeployMocks.s.sol:779-784).

(4) The script therefore asserts a post-condition of the PRE-story-073 topology, using a path the contract no longer takes. A green run is consistent with the streamer being entirely unwired, and proves nothing whatsoever about the index-4 repair.
evidence: git log --oneline -- script/interactions/TestBalancerDonation.s.sol => 4c5c3cd [story-070], 0bbbe8c [story-056], 090c37b [story-045.5]; none of story 073's commits appear. git log --grep=story-073 => 3fb4e34, d241e61, c054833. grep -n 'batchMint|collectNudge|nudgeStreamer' on the script returns only comment lines and `pooler.batchMinter()` reads (:76, :82, :87) — no batchMint call, no streamer reference. Source: :129 psm.buyGem(batchNFTMinterAddr, gemAmt); :135 require(usdcDelta == gemAmt, "donation USDC mismatch"), where usdcDelta is measured on usdc.balanceOf(batchNFTMinterAddr). Contrast DeployMocks.s.sol:779-784, which wires balancerPoolerV2.setNudgeStreamer(address(nudgeStreamer)) with the comment 'the donation reverts inside _psmDonate and _dispatch's try/catch swallows it — the mint succeeds but zero USDC ever reaches the batch minter (the exact silent breakage this story fixes)'. Story lines 505/538/539 verified as ticked in the current story file (840 lines).
recommendation: Either (a) rewrite TestBalancerDonation.s.sol to drive BalancerPoolerV2's OWN dispatch path end-to-end and assert on the NudgeStreamer buffer delta for (batchNFTMinter, USDC) — i.e. assert the thing the story repaired — or (b) untick lines 505 and 539 as they pertain to this script and record in Autonomous Decisions that test:balancer-donation is a PSM-route smoke test that does not cover the streamer leg. Do not leave it ticked as-is. Additionally, add the index-4 case to the story-072 feedback list with the explicit instruction that the assertion must be on the streamer buffer, not the batch minter's balance, since the cutover reproduces this topology on mainnet.

Nothing is broken; what is missing is the ability to DETECT it breaking.

severityRationale: LOW, matching the auditor's proposal. Weighed for QA and for Medium; Low is where the evidence sits. WHY NOT QA (i.e. why this is more than a bookkeeping nit). Three compounding facts. (1) FALSELY-EXHAUSTIVE CERTIFICATION, which under this repo's standing principle RAISES severity rather than lowering it: the story does not merely tick a box, it tells the reader at line 538 that this is 'the direct regression test for the streamer-unset breakage'. A future maintainer reading a green test:balancer-donation will conclude the index-4 streamer leg is proven. It is not; the assertion cannot fail for streamer reasons because the streamer is not on the path the script drives. (2) THE MASKED LEG IS THE SILENT ONE. Index-4 is precisely the leg where the pre-story breakage produced NO error — the source comment at DeployMocks.s.sol:779-781 says so in terms: 'the donation reverts inside _psmDonate and _dispatch's try/catch swallows it — the mint succeeds but zero USDC ever reaches the batch minter (the exact silent breakage this story fixes)'. So the one leg with no natural alarm is the one whose designated regression test is inert. That is a real detection gap, not a documentation nit. (3) THE SCRIPT IS NOT MERELY STALE, IT IS STRUCTURALLY MISALIGNED: it asserts `usdcDelta == gemAmt` against the batch minter's balance, which is the post-condition of the topology story 073 REPLACED. Under the new topology that equality holds for reasons unrelated to the feature, because the script performs the PSM buy itself. WHY NOT MEDIUM. Held down firmly, because overstatement is a documented rejection cause. (1) NOTHING IS BROKEN. The wiring is correct at this commit (DeployMocks.s.sol:784) and was independently confirmed on-chain by cast this run. There is no availability impact, no function impact and no value consequence — C4 Medium requires one of those, and the honest answer is that none exists. (2) The impact is strictly counterfactual: it materialises only if a future regression occurs AND the operator trusts this signal. A Medium may not be built on a contingency whose first conjunct has not happened. (3) LOCAL-ONLY in direct effect — this is a dev-chain interaction script on chainId 31337 with no mainnet artefact. It is nonetheless flagged LOCAL-ONLY-BUT-MASKS-MAINNET-RISK because story 072 inherits the same index-4 cutover and would inherit this test as its evidence of repair; the flag is the actionable part and is the reason the finding must reach the owner rather than a QA appendix. LAW-2 ROUTING IS THE POINT. Even at Low this is a story-faithfulness deviation — a ticked claim an artefact cannot support — so it is tagged faithfulness:true and routed to the spec-conformance report as F-01, visible to the owner, and is expressly NOT to be bundled into QA/gas noise.
classifierNotes: Kept SEPARATE from FAITH-002 and DEV-09. FAITH-001 = a specific named test is certified as covering a leg it structurally cannot reach (fix: rewrite the script to drive BalancerPoolerV2's own dispatch and assert on streamer buffer delta, or untick and say so). FAITH-002 = a checklist line certifying a manual confirmation with no evidence at all (fix: perform or untick). DEV-09 = the deploy script omits post-conditions (fix: add a verify:streams step). Three distinct guards, three distinct fixes; the standing rule is not to collapse distinct guards. SECOND-ORDER NOTE for the story-072 feedback list: whatever replaces this script must assert on the NudgeStreamer buffer delta for (batchMinter, USDC), not on the batch minter's USDC balance, or it will reproduce the same blindness under the new topology.

parkedItemsCarriedForward.title: ERC4626YieldStrategy.previewRedeem / previewDeposit view passthroughs still STATICCALL the underlying vault — the story-060 / YS-01 Tokemak fix is one-directional
parkedItemsCarriedForward.sourceVerification: Read against the TOP-LEVEL submodule HEAD lib/reflax-yield-vault (not a nested stale pin). :73-75 `return vault.previewDeposit(assets);` and :83-85 `return vault.previewRedeem(shares);`, both declared `external view` => Solidity emits STATICCALL. Twenty lines below, :110-115 credits principal via `vault.convertToAssets(sharesReceived)` with an in-source comment naming the exact hazard: 'Use convertToAssets (NOT previewRedeem): convertToAssets is ERC4626-mandated STATICCALL-safe, whereas some real vaults (e.g. Tokemak Autopools) mutate state inside previewRedeem and revert with StateChangeDuringStaticCall when called as an external view.' The authors therefore knew the hazard and hardened ONE call site.
parkedItemsCarriedForward.whyItMatters: Against a real Tokemak Autopool these two views revert for every caller, always; against MockAutoDOLA (plain un-overridden OZ ERC4626) they return a clean number, always. The local rig therefore reports green on the exact behaviour that already bricked this project's YS-swap suite. Blast radius today is UI/keeper reads (no first-party on-chain caller found), which is why this is parked for triage rather than asserted as a Medium.

secondaryGapsInTheSameMockSection: No maxRedeem/maxWithdraw check before `vault.redeem` in _disposeShares (:128-135): against a real Autopool with a liquid reserve below the request, user withdrawals brick. Locally impossible to reproduce.

MockAutoDOLA._updateYield() mints assets into the vault BEFORE super._deposit mints shares, so convertToAssets(sharesReceived) > amount and creditedPrincipal at :115 can EXCEED the deposited amount — the precise opposite of that line's stated intent. Any local invariant asserting 'principal is never over-credited' passes VACUOUSLY. Flagged because a vacuous-harness result is a known repeat failure mode in this repo.
